title: Tenant usage delta normalizer and idempotency protector
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: We see frequent small discrepancies between streaming token ingest and downstream billing snapshots caused by out-of-order events, duplicate replayed messages from edge relays, and late-arriving session close events. These deltas cause incorrect tenant invoices and manual adjustments.

Goal: Build a normalization stage (Delta Normalizer) that consumes raw ingestion streams, produces idempotent, time-window-aware tenant deltas, and emits single-source-of-truth change events into the billing sink. Provide an idempotency protection layer (dedupe cache + deterministic fencing keys) to make downstream processors safe to replay and retry.

Scope: - Streaming consumer in Kafka (raw-usage-topic) -> enrichment -> delta grouping -> deterministic key assignment -> dedupe cache (Scylla/Redis) -> Write to billing-change-topic. - Backfill job to repair historical windows where inconsistencies exceed threshold. - Console flags to control window size and caching TTL per customer tier.

Non-goals: Full rework of billing aggregation engine; this ticket focuses on producing stable canonical deltas.

Design decisions and trade-offs: - Use deterministic tenant-window keys (tenantId + hourBucket + sessionFingerprint) to avoid cross-window merging while limiting state size. This sacrifices fine-grained per-request attribution for simplicity and bounded-state guarantees. - Dedup cache stored in Scylla for persistent eviction guarantees; Redis used as a fast LRU for hot tenants. - Choose 10s compacting micro-batch with out-of-order tolerance of 3 minutes to balance latency and reconciliation complexity.

Observability: - Add per-tenant delta variance metric and small-signal alert if variance > 5% for 5 minutes. - Add end-to-end lineage tags in events so console can surface which pipeline produced final delta.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged; start 5% of tenants -> 25% -> 100% with shadow-run comparison metrics during ramp.
acceptance_criteria: Stable canonical delta events emitted to billing-change-topic with deterministic keys for >=99.98% of events
Dedup protection prevents double-crediting on replay for test tenancy scenarios
Backfill job corrects historical buckets where variance exceeds configured threshold and produces audit report
Dashboard displays per-tenant delta variance and pipeline lag within console-analytics
Automated test coverage for deterministic key generation and eviction policies
implementation_notes: Kafka consumer will be implemented as a Flink job using exactly-once semantics where possible; fallback to idempotent writes when exactly-once cannot be guaranteed
Use SHA1(session_prefix) truncated to 64 bits for sessionFingerprint to keep keys compact
Dedup TTL defaults to 72 hours for standard tenants; dedicated tenants use 7-day TTL configurable via console
Backfill job implemented as Spark batch reading raw S3 dumps, producing repair events to billing-change-topic with repair metadata
